hazard: Misleading layout causing pedestrians to cross incorrectly

promises.quote: A zebra crossing was installed on 15 March 2016, south of, but close to, the junction, to provide an additional crossing from the Millennium Village area to the existing primary school, and a safer crossing route between Pilot Busway and West Parkside.

concerns.quote: the layout of Pilot Busway and the neighbouring road (West Parkside) is unusual: they run side by side; West Parkside consists of a single carriageway in each direction; Pilot Busway consists of a single dedicated bus lane in each direction. The evidence was that this layout could mislead road users (pedestrians and motorists) into believing that this is a standard dual carriageway. Ordinary traffic has been seen in the dedicated busway, and pedestrians could be misled into looking the wrong way

promises.quote: Subsequent to this visit, additional louvres were fitted on 13 October 2017 to two further green figure light aspects on the Pentonville Road crossing, including on the north side of the crossing (see Figure 2), to reduce the likelihood of pedestrians crossing when they were not invited
promises.summary: additional louvres fitted to reduce pedestrian crossing risk

concerns.quote: No road markings indicating the direction pedestrians should look when crossing
concerns.hazard: pedestrians may not know which way to look when crossing

links.explanation: Both reports highlight that the road layout can cause pedestrians to look in the wrong direction when crossing, creating a safety risk. The earlier report cites the unusual side‑by‑side busway/road layout as misleading, while the later report notes the absence of road markings indicating the correct looking direction.
